title: Handling Errors Across Application Layers knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Handling Errors Across Application Layers?
options: Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Preserve causes and error codes, log structured context without secrets, and use diagnostics before guessing at a fix.
questions.answer_key: Preserve causes and error codes, log structured context without secrets, and use diagnostics before guessing at a fix.
questions.explanation: Preserve causes and error codes, log structured context without secrets, and use diagnostics before guessing at a fix. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Handling Errors Across Application Layers?
questions.explanation: “Propagating errors” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Handling Errors Across Application Layers implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
